creator: Elephants in Rooms - Ken LaCorte
title: Here was the world Hitler planned
full_text:
What if Hitler had
really won
World War II?
Listen, I've seen
a few videos on this
topic, and they were all
a bit fantastical.
More of a dystopian
novel than a clear
view of history.
So it's not so much
The Man in the High
Castle, where Nazis
rule the United
States, but a much more
realistic
look at how
a few individual events
could have changed the course of
events in
Hitler's favor, and what the
subsequent
reality might have been. Because
Hitler, as he often
did, told
us exactly what he would do.
He recorded this in detail
using maps.
And the real question
is whether
this world could
hold together and what
could stop it
. I'm Ken LeCour, and
today's challenge is to
understand a
realistic
alternative
history that we might
actually
encounter. Let's start with
how
close he came,
because
Allied victory was not
certain. Then
consider the plan
he planned
to build on the
victory. We will then
look at some of the
problems with the Third
Reich and how it
may have been built
to collapse.
Finally, we
will consider the problem of
America, because it
stood between Hitler and
global
domination. So,
first let's
see
how close
he came to
winning the war. I
mean, in
our modern thinking, the
Nazis were
doomed from the
start, and the good
guys were always supposed to
win. And it's a
comforting story, but
it's simply
not true.
At least, there were
at least three
moments when a different
decision could have given
Hitler all of Europe.
Let's take the end of
May 1940.
France is falling faster
than anyone could have
imagined. The British
army is pinned down on the
beach at Dunkirk, and a
serious faction in
their war
cabinet is pressuring
Churchill to make a
deal with
Germany. This
argument had some
merit. I mean,
Britain
was on its own. Their army
was trapped, and the fighting
looked like
national
suicide. If this
faction had won this
argument, the war in
the West would have ended
before the
United
States even came into being. Or September
1940, the Battle of
Britain. British
pilots are dying faster
than they can be replaced
, airfields
are collapsing, and the entire
force is close to
collapse. If the
Royal Air Force
collapses,
Germany will own
the skies over the English Channel, and an
invasion of
Britain
turns from
fantasy into something
real. Or the winter of 1941
near Moscow. The
German offensive on
the capital, which
progressed throughout the autumn.
In mid-October, the
Soviet government
panicked and began
evacuation. They
loaded
documents onto trains.
Government buildings were
prepared for
demolition. By early
December, German
reconnaissance
units had reached the
very outskirts of Moscow
. Close enough to
see it through binoculars.
About 15-20 miles
from the Kremlin. The entire
Eastern Front
was teetering on a
razor's edge. And Hitler, the
same man who
came so close,
also made
mistakes that
saved us. He
stopped his tanks at
Dunkirk and allowed the
British army
to slip away. He
invaded the
Soviet Union
while Britain was still
fighting, something
every general
since
Napoleon could have warned him against. And after
Pearl Harbor, he
was not obligated
by Japan
to declare war on the
United States,
but he
did it anyway. Hitler
came terrifyingly close to victory
in Europe. And if so,
what were his
plans? Here is the plan.
Historian Gerhard
Weinberg, who
wrote a prominent
history of the war,
explained
Hitler's plans in detail. They
happened in stages
. The first stage was
Europe. First,
annex Denmark,
Norway, Sweden, and
Finland as joint
German territory.
Turn France,
Britain, and Ireland
into controlled
puppet states
and reduce Spain and
Portugal to
satellite states. The second
stage was the real
prize–the East. I
mean, this is where it
stops being a
conquest and becomes
something else, even
uglier. I
don't mean
ruling the people, but
destroying them. The plan
was called "General
Plan East", a
master plan for the
East. It envisaged the
extermination or
deportation of over 30
million people in
Poland, the Baltic States,
Belarus, Ukraine, and
parts of
Russia. The percentages themselves are
impressive.
Over 80% of Poles were
marked for
eviction, about 75% of
Belarusians. The Jews
were marked for
complete destruction.
Others were to
be deported to the east
or worked to
death. The Slavs were to be
pushed east to
Siberia or kept as
slaves. Then the Germans
were to intervene and
populate the devastated
land. Along with this
came the "Famine Plan,
" which is
indeed mentioned and
is one of the
scariest things
I have encountered in
this research.
But before we
get to that, I
want to talk about
today's
sponsor and
occupational therapy. I've
only done this once in
my life for
marriage
counseling. And for
someone like me,
I just didn't
like the logistics
. I mean
trying to find the
right person,
then the trip there, and
then the experience of
waiting, all
before you
even start. And
when one
consultant doesn't
work, it's
even inconvenient
to change him. BetterHelp, our
sponsor today
, solves all of this. You
take a short
test and they
match you with a
licensed
therapist. No
need to
commute, no
waiting room. You can
conduct sessions
by phone, video,
even text
message, whatever
suits your
schedule and your
comfort level. This
allows you to find
a therapist far beyond
your
immediate
area of ​​residence. And
if the selection doesn't
suit you, you can
change it at any
time, without additional
costs or awkward
conversations. Over 6
million people
have used
BetterHelp services to
date. So, if
one of the obstacles between
you and therapy was
hassle with how the
process works, or
finding someone in your
area, this will solve
that problem for you.
Go to
betterhelp.com/kendallacourt and
get 10% off for a
month. Okay,
back to the war
and Hitler's
famine plan. The architect
was an
agricultural
official named
Herbert Bakke. And
the logic was coldly
practical.
Germany wanted
food grown in the
Soviet granary to
feed its
own army and people
. So the plan was to
redirect this
food to the west.
Planners
wrote down this figure.
It was expected that 20
to 30 million people
in the occupied East
would die of starvation. I
mean, the
Nazis understood that,
and it was part of the
policy. His
model for all of
this was the United
States, and he directly
stated this in his
writings. In fact, he
considered the Slavs, whom he
planned to cleanse
from the land, to be the new
Native
Americans. He
looked at what
European
settlers had done in
America and was going to
use that
as a reference point. The
resettlement plans were
very specific.
Crimea was to be
cleared and
handed over to German
settlers. Great
highways would
push East into the
conquered lands, and
along them would be
built new
German cities, all of
them
built with slave
labor. The third stage
was to take place
later. After
conquering Europe,
Hitler hoped to
reclaim Germany's old
African colonies
and
help
redistribute the
continent under
Axis control.
He even
counted on
regimes like apartheid
South Africa as
sympathetic
partners, not
enemies. So, the
Nazi genocide
that we saw
took the lives of over 12
million people, but
that was only the first
act. A full plan for
the East would have included
tens of millions more
in addition to this, in a
deliberate,
organized
genocide that would
span the entire
continent. As usual
with the Nazis, this was not a
crowd of thugs
who would solve
various issues on the fly
. Heinrich Himmler
ran the machine and
even tasked
professors with
developing
racial classification systems
that would decide
who would live, who would die,
and who would become slaves. It
was genocide with
notes. While all
this was being planned,
Hitler was moving forward
with his
favorite
architect,
Albert Speer,
on a project
they called "
Germany." It was a
complete restructuring of
Berlin as the capital of the
world. The
centerpiece was a hall designed
to seat 180,000
people, with a dome
larger than
St. Peter's Basilica in Rome
and a triumphal
arch
large enough to
house the
Arc de Triomphe several times over.
Their goal
was also to change religion.
We tend to imagine
the Nazis as simply
cynical
about religion, willing
to use
the church when it was
convenient and ignore it
otherwise. But
they planned to
destroy her as a
potential opposition.
In Germany,
there was even a name for the
intermediate step –
positive
Christianity. This
sounded harmless,
but in practice it
meant getting rid
of those parts of the faith
that contradicted
Nazi doctrine
, downplaying
the divinity of
Christ, erasing his
Jewishness
,
minimizing the Old
Testament, and
linking what
remained to the cult
of the Fuhrer. This
was advertised as a
more Germanic
Christianity, but the
goal was to subjugate
the church to the state. In
the long
term, they
wanted
Christianity to
disappear from
Germany completely.
There is now a well-known 30-
point program of the so-
called national
Reich Church, which is
quoted everywhere. Bibles
are replaced with "Mein
Kampf," crosses
are replaced with
swastikas, but the wartime Gestapo
traced it to
one fanatic, so
it wasn't official
policy, and the state
never actually
adopted it. But
there is no doubt that
Alfred Rosenberg, the
Nazi Party's chief architect of
religion,
intended to destroy
German
Christianity and
eventually replace
it with something
built on blood
and nation. Before the war, he
was already
responsible for the
party's philosophical education, which meant
shaping
the worldview of
stormtroopers,
Hitler Youth, and
rank-and-file Nazis.
Church leaders in the 1930s
saw his
rise to power and
openly worried
that the state had just
placed an
anti-Christian
crusader
in charge of the
soul of the nation, and they were not
wrong. And the church was
already sagging. In 1938,
about 90% of
Protestant
pastors in Germany
took a personal
oath of allegiance to
Hitler. I
mean, the wording
was pretty harsh.
I swear that I will be
faithful and obedient to the
Führer of the German
Reich and nation,
Adolf Hitler, so
help me God.
So, the regime didn't
have to break
the church by force, because
intimidation was already
working well enough. But even
if Hitler had won
on the battlefield, the
government he created
had some
fundamental
problems and was in many
ways
built for
destruction. Start with
money. The Nazi
economy was...It
was a
time bomb, and the
regime knew it.
Germany chronically
lacked the
foreign currency
needed for
raw materials, lurching
from one currency
crisis to another
throughout the 1930s. The
rearmament boom,
tanks, planes,
uniforms...They
worked on
Mefo bills,
government debt
receipts, which
were essentially
printed
promises to pay
later. These promises
were counted down
, with
repayments due
between 1939 and 1942
. So war
was necessary if
Hitler wanted to
continue to
evade the
collectors. There was a
four-year plan
that was supposed to make
Germany
self-sufficient, but
it failed. Their
economy was based
on conquests. They
had to constantly
absorb territories
to plunder
resources, seize
gold, and incubate
slave labor. If
they stopped
conquering,
mathematics would
collapse. However,
it wouldn't fall apart overnight
. There was a
less acceptable view from
economists
working in Great
Britain in the late
1930s. Thomas
Balogh and Claude Gibot
refuted the
popular idea that
Germany was about
to break up. In their
view, the Nazi
system was
harsher than
people wanted to believe, and it was
held together
by crude
authoritarian
control. So, from
their perspective, a
victorious Germany
could hold out
much longer than
we would like to think
. But perhaps a more
pressing problem
for the Third Reich
was keeping the
conquered
population under
control.
Look at
Yugoslavia. Germany
had to keep
over half a million
Axis troops
just to hold on. And
they, as always,
handled it
brutally. They
were ordered
to execute 50 to 100
civilians for
every
German soldier killed.
It was brutal, but
this repression only
strengthened the resistance, as
genocide often
makes the problem worse.
When the only
alternative is
death, people don't
always lie down. They
fight because they have
nothing left
to lose. Mass
murders give
every able-bodied
person a reason to pick up
a rifle. This
doesn't
always happen, but sometimes it
does. Now
spread that across the entire
conquered
continent, to those
destined for
slavery, deportation,
or death, and the Nazis
could put out fires
in many places. In
addition to this
chaos, they have always
had serious
political strife. The
Nazi
leadership was a pit of vipers
even in
peacetime. Himmler,
Goering, Goebbels –
they always fought
for power. A movement
built on
one strong
leader has an obvious
problem. Hitler
even tried
to resolve the issue of
his succession
as early as 1941. He
signed an official
decree designating
Göring as his
heir. But
after 4 years, he
stripped him of all
these titles and ordered his
arrest for
treason. Then
he did the same to
Himmler a few
days before his own
death. The two
men he had
officially appointed as
his heirs were
expelled before the end. And
the problems were not only
internal. On
paper, Germany and
Japan were
partners. They
even divided the
world among themselves by
drawing a line
along the 70th meridian
. Germany
claimed everything
to the west of it,
Japan to the east. But no
one seriously
thought in Berlin that
these borders
would survive the war.
Once Japan
had done the dirty
work in China and
the Pacific, the plan was to
turn against
them as well. I mean,
when you created a movement
based on the
racial superiority of the
Aryan race,
the Japanese simply did not
fit that
description. The regime tried to
get around this by labeling
the Japanese as
honorary Aryans and
hoping that no
one would
laugh. And some
theorists even
went further, tying
themselves in knots,
claiming that
the Japanese were an
Aryan people of
the East who
developed independently
. But even Japan did not
fall for this
deception. It
refused
to hand over Jewish
communities in its
territories. It
completely rejected
Nazi racial
doctrine and waged its
own war,
largely independently of
Berlin. The victorious
Axis does not give you a
stable new
order. She gives you
two weary
conquerors,
staring at each
other across this
meridian, each
plotting to betray the
other. Winning the
war would not
end wars. She would
simply decide who
would fight whom
next. So, listen,
now is the time
to point out that if I get
any major
facts wrong here, let
me know in the comments. I'll
address this in a
pinned
comment below. There
you will also see
sources and
research notes
. Okay, Hitler
thought America was a
joke. And he never
took seriously
the problem of America that
awaited him after the
war. He called
Americans a race of
mongrels and suggested
that the country would rot
from within long before
it could
threaten them. As late as 1944
, when
American tanks,
planes, and men
were doing the hard
work in Western
Europe, Hitler was still
more worried about
Britain than the
United States. And the
economic and
military production
capacity of the
United States
was enormous. I
mean, numbers
that were bigger
than Germany and
most of
Europe combined.
In 5 years, America
produced over 300,000
airplanes, 100,000
ships, and millions of
vehicles
. But
Hitler's contempt
was accompanied by
theory. America was
spiritually weak. In
his opinion, it was
dependent on
consumer conveniences
, divided
by immigrants, and
corrupted by
Jewish influence.
He believed that such a
society would not
withstand any
serious stress and would
eventually collapse on its own
. However,
his military
planners
were not so
sure and had their
own ideas. One of
the programs was
nicknamed "
Bomber
America". This was a
serious attempt
to develop a
long-range aircraft
that could take off
from Europe, hit New
York, and then simply
never return. Their
V2 rocket scientists
created a sketch of a
two-stage
monster, which some
called the
America rocket, and it was an
intercontinental
rocket designed
to launch in Europe
and land on the
East Coast.
As an alternative, they
even planned
to tow missiles
across the Atlantic behind
submarines
if
intercontinental
ships wouldn't fly.
Each of these plans
aimed to solve the same
problem. Germany
simply could not
move an army
across the Atlantic
Ocean. I mean,
even if they
could bomb
cities, you can't
occupy a country that you can't
reach with troops.
This is why most
historians believe
that the post-war
reality would be a
kind of
permanent
Cold War with a
Europe
controlled by
the Nazis on one
side and an isolated
and untouchable
United States
on the other. However, such a
confrontation would
probably not leave
America
intact from
within, because a
democracy locked
in a permanent
Cold War with a
continent-sized fascist state
would instill fear here.
This would probably be a
more extreme
version of the Cold
War with the Soviet
Union. And that would have kept
America with a large
army, McCarthyism,
red scares,
and nuclear
drills in schools.
Against a more powerful,
brutal
Nazi regime,
America would have been
fixated on that
threat for as long as
it existed. How would
this affect the
United States?
You know, it's not hard
to imagine how oaths of
allegiance
turn into
loyalty tests, or how
extraordinary
powers become
more ordinary
powers. And
the line between the
security state and the
police
state
is becoming more blurred every year.
Internally, America
could look like a
different country than the one that
entered the war.
But at least for
a while there would be an ace
that only the
United States had.
Nuclear weapons. The irony
is that
German scientists were
the first to achieve
this through pure
science. In 1938,
German scientists
split the atom in
Berlin, discovering
nuclear fission. Then
they moved away from
it. In 1942,
Hitler's people told him
that the bomb would not appear
at any convenient
time, so the
priority was lowered. I
mean, the
German teams
never achieved a sustainable
chain reaction.
They didn't so much
lose the nuclear
race as simply
move away from it. By
1948, the United
States had about 50
atomic bombs.
Germany, even in a
scenario of complete
victory, almost
certainly had
none, at least for
a while. So,
Germany owns
the continent, America
owns the nuclear
bombs. But would
they use them
? Well, as we saw in
Japan, and I made a whole
video about it, the
American
military, they didn't
have the particular
moral qualms
about nuclear bombs that
we have today.
Neither Truman nor the generals
had any particular
discussions on this
matter. They were
happy to have a big
bomb to
end a war that
was killing Americans,
and they used it
as soon as they could. The
only real variable
in this scenario is
when
Hitler's victory will occur.
If this happens
early, before the
United States
invades Europe, there will be
no
war left that can be
ended with the bomb, and
no reason to
use it.
If it happens
later, after years of
fighting and thousands of
American deaths, Truman
will probably use
it as soon as he can, just as
he
did with Japan.
However, this nuclear
advantage does not last
forever. Once
Germany builds its
own bombs, the US
loses its
unilateral influence
and you're back
in a stalemate.
I came away from this less
convinced that the Nazis were
doomed, and more
convinced of
how little it
mattered. So, a
successful Germany in
Europe, look, wouldn't have
lasted a thousand
years. She simply
had too many
obstacles and problems
within herself. So
this Reich would collapse at some
point,
but it could be 10
years, it could be 50
years. And this gap
means tens of
millions of dead
people. So, being
doomed is ultimately
not the same as being
stopped as
it was. We know
that freedom was not
inevitable. It was chosen by
real people in
real moments who
could have chosen differently
. And, if we look
at the past more
sensibly, Germany
might have won
Europe, but America would have been the
favorite to
win the century.
History has a habit of
creating questions
that sometimes seem
obvious until you
delve deeper into them
. World
War II, of course, and the
modern Middle
East as well. And there,
one thing I
could never understand about the
war in Gaza is that,
despite the fact that
most of them were
forced to flee
their homes, no
Arab country
ever
offered to take in
any of their
refugees. In fact, it
was quite the
opposite. The answer is not
simple. I mean,
it's connected to the
history of many
countries over
different generations. This
video explains it all,
and I think you
might find it interesting. Hey,
thank you very much for your time.
I hope this
look into the past was
worth your time.
Until the next
meeting.

notes.note: The economist's name is misstated. There is no economist named "Claude Gibot" — the British economist who challenged predictions of Nazi Germany's economic collapse alongside Thomas Balogh was Claude W. Guillebaud, author of "The Economic Recovery of Germany" (1939).
notes.claim: Thomas Balogh and Claude Guillebaud were economists working in Great Britain in the late 1930s who refuted the popular idea that Germany was about to break up economically.
notes.context_quote: Thomas Balogh and Claude Gibot refuted the popular idea that Germany was about to break up.
notes.context_paragraph: There was a less acceptable view from economists working in Great Britain in the late 1930s. Thomas Balogh and Claude Gibot refuted the popular idea that Germany was about to break up.

sources.quote: Claude William Guillebaud... was an influential British economist, at the Faculty of Economics, University of Cambridge
sources.explanation: Confirms the existence and identity of the British economist Claude W. Guillebaud.
Confirms he authored the book cited in the note.

sources.quote: Claude Guillebaud (which ought to be pronounced to rhyme with "keel-bow")
sources.explanation: Provides the pronunciation, which explains how a transcript might mishear the name as "Gibot."

sources.quote: Two British economists writing in the late 1930s, Thomas Balogh and Claude Guillebaud, challenged this narrative... both men concluded that the Nazi economic system would not collapse in the near future.
sources.explanation: Supports the claim that Guillebaud worked alongside Balogh to challenge the consensus regarding a German economic collapse.

notes.note: The Bibles-for-Mein Kampf, crosses-for-swastikas plan was not the work of an obscure fanatic uncovered by the Gestapo. It was a 30-point program publicly released by Alfred Rosenberg, a top Nazi ideologue and Reich Minister for the Occupied Eastern Territories.
notes.claim: The wartime Gestapo traced the 30-point National Reich Church program to one individual fanatic, and it was never official state policy.
notes.context_quote: the wartime Gestapo traced it to one fanatic, so it wasn't official policy, and the state never actually adopted it.
notes.context_paragraph: Bibles are replaced with "Mein Kampf," crosses are replaced with swastikas, but the wartime Gestapo traced it to one fanatic, so it wasn't official policy, and the state never actually adopted it.

sources.quote: Dr. Alfred Rosenberg, long the antireligious polemist of modern Germany and the protagonist of the “new national church,” has just released for publication a thirty-point program
sources.explanation: This identifies Alfred Rosenberg as the author of the 30-point program mentioned in the note.

sources.quote: 18. The National Reich Church will remove from the altars of all churches the Bible, the cross and religious objects. 19. In their place will be set that which must be venerated by the German people and therefore is by God, our most saintly book, “Mein Kampf,” and to the left of this a sword.
sources.explanation: These points (18 and 19) confirm the note's description of replacing Bibles and crosses with Mein Kampf.

sources.quote: 30. On the day of the foundation of the National Reich Church the Christian cross shall be removed from all churches, cathedrals and chapels inside the frontiers of the Reich and its colonies and will be replaced by the symbol of invincible Germany—the swastika.
sources.explanation: This point (30) confirms the plan to replace crosses with swastikas.

sources.quote: Alfred Rosenberg (January 12, 1893–October 16, 1946) was one of the most influential Nazi intellectuals. In the course of his career, he held a number of important German state and Nazi Party posts.
sources.explanation: Confirms Rosenberg was a top ideologue, not an obscure fanatic.

sources.quote: On July 17, 1941, Hitler appointed him Reich Minister for the Occupied Eastern Territories [Reichsminister für die besetzten Ostgebiete]
sources.explanation: Confirms his official title as Reich Minister, as stated in the note.
